Event: `8ce337106b2b4ace92a901168d912ad2` · 2026-10-19T10:21:32Z

> STEWARD10 shape: the ruled mechanism does not map onto the code; here is the steward-only form I am building, proceeding unless you object. Detail: .worktrees/STEWARD10/.tmp/STEWARD10/shape.md.
> 
> Facts: (1) DestroyBudget is no step of STEWARD5's queue (that holds connections); it runs inline in drive.rs step() in the Exited event, an end_lease's end batch, and forget(). Nothing to cancel under the lock. (2) The steward never sees the kernel's BudgetRef id (Machine::budget_id returns the index; no rt call reads one). Its identity is its own record plus the deadline it minted. (3) time.rs: expiry runs at every kernel entry first, so a budget with deadline d is destroyed at the first entry at or after d, never before. (4) Only the loop initiates installs in the steward's table (the thread's disconnect installs nothing; watchers/readers receive only what the loop sends them, inside its blocking send).
> 
> Rule: Made::Budget carries its deadline. A destroy by index follows a fresh kernel.now() read t immediately before it, no install between. t >= d: the kernel took it; drop the record, no destroy. t < d, Ok: the right budget. t < d, BadHandle: re-read now(); >= d is the deadline passing inside the window (benign); < d a real failure. WrongObject is a failure. The `BadHandle if !running` tolerance goes. Same rule in forget() (the crossing's budget is destroyed there with the error ignored: the silent form reachable too). Also covers an end_lease served after d but before the exit notice, which a cancel at the notice could not.
> 
> Host tests: index recycled for a new budget before the notice, the new budget's liveness in the fake kernel the verdict; recycled for a connection, no WrongObject; end_lease in the window; end_lease and sequential deadline unchanged. No kernel change.
